coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 6 units (domain root + 08.01..08.05), 32 files — matches the expected count exactly. Every file was read in full via sandbox line-numbered dumps; no sampling. Rubric applicability: dimensions 2 (Persona Specificity), 5 (Success Measurability) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are N/A on every unit — personas are owned by meta/personas.md and explicitly 'never redefined here — referenced only' (domain index line 87), there is no success-metrics section anywhere in an ideation domain unit, and per the brief dimension 6 belongs to meta/competitive-landscape.md rather than to domain or leaf files. Dimension 4 (Constraint Explicitness) is also N/A: its axes (budget, timeline, team size, compliance) are project-level and live in meta/constraints.md; where this domain states constraints it does so with hard numbers (8.64 MB/channel-minute, 20/50/100 ppm, 5-25 ms round-trip, 1/5/20 ms tiers). Applicable checkpoints per unit are therefore dimensions 1, 3, 7, 8 (4 rubric checkpoints) PLUS one checkpoint per implementer-simulation finding (dimension 0), per scoring.md's rule that simulation gaps 'count toward the ambiguity score'. Dimension-0 findings are scored as their own checkpoints rather than folded into a rubric dimension, because the rubric has no internal-consistency dimension and folding a blocking contradiction into 'Feature Completeness' would misattribute it. Cross-references were followed off-domain where a claim depended on them: ideation/moscow-ledger.md and specs/feature-ledger.md were opened only to verify quoted MoSCoW placements (finding #011). No file under .memory/wiki/specs/audits/ outside run5/ was opened. Overall raw ambiguity for the domain: 12.0 points / 36 applicable checkpoints = 33.3%. The tree is of unusually high quality — 08.05.01, 08.05.02, 08.05.04 and 08.07 are near-exemplary, with arithmetic instead of adjectives and adversarial DT annotations that reject their own best ideas. The findings cluster in two places: (a) statements that were superseded by a later pass but never amended in the file that carries them, and (b) `[PENDING — Step 5]` / `Deferred To: MoSCoW` markers left pointing at pipeline stages that have since completed, which the domain itself acknowledges elsewhere ('Step 5 has since completed', domain index Q-05/Q-06) and which it re-pointed correctly in most — but not all — files.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer reading the domain index must decide whether an overdub's provenance record carries the same certainty as a live session's, or a lower graded one. The index says the same; three other files say lower.
findings.claim: The domain index asserts that Overdub Mode 'carries the provenance (08.05.04) intact', which is flatly contradicted — with no marker on the index statement — by 08.07 D-04, by the domain's own CX-07, and by 08.05.04's corrected grade model. 08.07 explicitly names the index as the file carrying the uncorrected claim, and the Step 6 CX pass (dated 2026-07-18, two days after the index) recorded the correction in the CX file but never amended the index.
findings.evidence: realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-index.md:47 — 'Overdub needs file storage and background jobs — no media infrastructure. And it carries the provenance (08.05.04) intact.' And realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-index.md:122 (D-05) — 'Overdub also runs on the locked stack and carries the provenance intact.' Contradicted by 08.07-overdub-mode.md:353 (D-04) — '**Provenance is captured without real-time transport, at a stated grade — NOT identically to a live session** … The breadth pass claimed identical certainty; that was an overclaim (DT-08).' And by realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-cx.md:23 (CX-07) — 'Overdub yields a **different provenance grade**: delivery-certainty (a file arrived), not performance-certainty (a human observed playing).' And by 08.07-overdub-mode.md:333 — 'This file cannot edit 08.05.04, its index, or the domain index (D-05 and domain-index D-04 both carry the uncorrected claim). Step 6 must propagate the grade concept or the thesis claim for domain 08 is overstated at its most load-bearing point.'
findings.failure_scenario: A downstream reader (or /create-prd, which reads the domain index first) plans the attendance record as a single-certainty artifact and drops the `delivered-by` / `observed-playing` / `counter-attested` grade dimension. The domain's entire thesis link rests on that distinction — CX-07 escalates the grade to the global CX as a new cross-cut serving domains 02, 08 and 09, and 02.04.02 consumes it as the top rung of its tier ladder. Building the ungraded version silently upgrades every solo overdub to the evidentiary weight of an observed live performance, which is the exact 'verified false credit' failure 08.05.04 DT-02 says is worse than an unverified one.

findings.claim: The domain Role Matrix grants the Musician only 'Read-only' access across sub-domain 08.03, but 08.03's own Role Matrix grants the Musician 'Full' on 08.03.03 and 'Config' on 08.03.04. Every other row of the domain Role Matrix is a max-rollup of its children; this row is neither a max nor a min.
findings.evidence: realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-index.md:93 — '| 08.03 Remote Monitoring & Session Attendance | 👁️ Read-only | ✅ Full | ⚙️ Config | ❌ None |'. Contradicted by 08.03-remote-monitoring-session-attendance-index.md:41-42 — '| 08.03.03 Live Listener Feedback & Timestamped Notes | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ❌ None | ❌ None |' and '| 08.03.04 Monitoring Trust & Playback Context | ⚙️ Config | 👁️ Read-only | ⚙️ Config | ❌ None |'. Confirmed by 08.03.03-live-listener-feedback-notes.md:21 — 'Musician | Full | Can leave notes as a listener'. The max-rollup convention holds on every other row: 08.01 children are Full/Full/Read-only → domain row 'Full'; 08.04 children are Read-only/Full/Full → 'Full'; 08.05 children are Full/Read-only/Full/Full → 'Full'.
findings.failure_scenario: An access-control model derived from the domain Role Matrix (the coarser, more visible table, and the one a downstream IA shard is most likely to lift wholesale) makes Musicians read-only across all of remote monitoring. Musicians then cannot leave timestamped notes — the capability 08.03.03's Role Lens describes in detail ('a bandmate attending a mix they are not playing on') — and cannot declare their own playback context in 08.03.04, silently deleting one persona from two features.

findings.forcedInvention: Whether an un-uploaded pass is retried forever or abandoned when its overdub request expires.
findings.claim: 08.07 bounds upload resumption by the request's expiry and attributes that bound to 08.05.01 D-03, but D-03 states the opposite — indefinite retry with no dead-letter and no bound other than the app being reopened.
findings.evidence: 08.05.01-local-first-multitrack-capture.md:336 (D-03) — 'Uploads are resumable and never abandoned — backoff 2 s → 5 min cap, indefinite, resumes on next open, no dead-letter'; and line 151-153 — 'There is no dead-letter, because a dead-lettered take is a lost take.' Contradicted by 08.07-overdub-mode.md:248 — 'Resumption is not time-boxed short — a take abandoned at 90% is how work is lost. **Persists until the request expires.**' And 08.07-overdub-mode.md:321 (DT-13) — 'the answer is 08.05.01 D-03 — resumable, chunked, surviving app close and time-boxed only by the request's expiry' — a bound D-03 does not contain.
findings.failure_scenario: A player accepts an overdub request, records four passes, and their laptop stays shut past the Friday deadline. Under D-03 the passes upload whenever the app next opens, months later, and remain evidence of work done — which 08.07's own cancellation edge row wants ('Your passes are still yours — deliver them for the record?'). Under 08.07's expiry bound the upload queue is dropped at expiry and the passes are stranded locally forever. Two implementers reading the two files build opposite retention behaviour for the same queue, and the losing case destroys the delivery record the provenance grade depends on.

findings.forcedInvention: Whether the shared click re-aligns live when latency drifts during a take, or holds its alignment and lets the click drift out.
findings.claim: A product choice the file itself labels 'genuine' is left at `[PENDING — Step 5]` with no owner, and Step 5 has completed. No open question in 08.01.03 covers it — Q-01 is the symmetric/conductor model choice, Q-02 is conductor-drop succession, Q-03 is whether the click is recorded as an alignment reference.
findings.evidence: 08.01.03-shared-clock-click-countin.md:56 — '| Latency drifts during a take, breaking alignment | `[PENDING — Step 5]` — whether the click re-aligns live (which itself is an audible timing change) or holds and lets it drift. Both are bad; this is a genuine product choice. | `[PENDING]` |'. Step 5 completion is recorded in realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-index.md:134 (Q-05) — 'Step 5 has since completed without sourcing them' — and at Q-06 — 'Step 5 has since completed and neither merge was taken'. Sibling rows in the same file were re-pointed correctly: 08.01.03 Q-02 was 'Re-pointed from the completed `/ideate-discover` Step 5' to `/create-prd-architecture`; this row was not.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer building the click engine picks live re-alignment because it keeps the click 'correct'. Every latency excursion during a take then produces an audible timing step in every performer's headphones mid-performance — the exact class of damage 08.01.03 D-02 forbids for the timing model ('Shifting the timing reference while people play is destructive to the take and to the players'). The alternative implementer picks hold-and-drift and the click silently walks away from the ensemble. Both ship; neither was chosen.

findings.claim: Whether a mid-session red playability verdict interrupts players (as opposed to only notifying the Producer) is deferred to Step 5 in two files, with no owner in either, after Step 5 completed. Both files state the notification to the Producer is settled and leave the player half open.
findings.evidence: 08.01-latency-budget-playability-cx.md:36 (CX-01 synthesis Q4) — 'A verdict transition from green to red mid-session must notify the Producer (they are the one billing). Whether it notifies players is `[PENDING — Step 5]`.' And 08.01.02-playability-verdict-tempo-ceiling.md:62 — '| Verdict flips red mid-session | Producer is notified (they are billing). Whether players are interrupted is `[PENDING — Step 5]` — a modal mid-take is its own kind of damage. | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` |'. Neither 08.01.02's nor the index's open-question table carries the item; 08.01.02 Q-01 is the threshold table, Q-02 is the MoSCoW keep-or-cut, Q-03 is the commercial consequence.
findings.failure_scenario: The behaviour is a straight collision with a rule the domain states elsewhere as absolute — 08.03.03 D-02 and 08.05.03 both hold that nothing may interrupt a performer mid-take — yet the file explicitly leaves interruption open. An implementer resolving it from the notification requirement alone ships a modal that fires in front of a performer while they are playing, destroying the take to report a network fact the Producer already has.

findings.forcedInvention: Whether latency re-measurement is rate-limited, and whether variance across runs is shown or the user is left free to cherry-pick their best number.
findings.claim: Both the behaviour and the user-facing result for a named abuse case are `[PENDING]`, deferred to a completed stage, with no owner and no covering open question (08.01.01's three questions are directional delay, telemetry retention, and peer-ledger consent).
findings.evidence: 08.01.01-latency-measurement-decomposition.md:56 — '| User re-measures obsessively, hunting a better number | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — whether to rate-limit, and whether to show variance across runs rather than encourage cherry-picking the best one. | `[PENDING]` |'. This matters against the file's own D-02 — 'Fail-closed: an unmeasured or unreachable link renders `Unknown`, never a green or a zero … A false green in this domain costs a paid session' — and against 08.02.02's dependence on measurement history: 08.02.02-route-aware-radius-correction.md:29 — 'A single bad probe during a transient network event must not permanently shrink someone's radius, and a single lucky probe must not inflate it.'
findings.failure_scenario: With no rate limit and no variance display, a musician re-measures until a favourable number appears and that number becomes the standing verdict shown to a Producer staffing a paid session. The same cherry-picked probes feed 08.02.02's correction loop, which 08.02.02 D-02 requires to be confidence-weighted — but the confidence model cannot distinguish twenty honest probes from twenty attempts at one, so a self-selected best case inflates a radius and a session is booked on a link that will not hold.

findings.forcedInvention: The confidence model, the sample threshold at which a measured radius supersedes a prediction, the decay rate on old probes, and whether corrections are keyed per-route or per-peer.
findings.claim: The feature's own Behavior section calls the arbitration rule 'the substance of this feature' and marks all four of its parameters `[PENDING — Step 5]` with no owner, after Step 5 completed — while the States table depends on a Learning→Measured transition that only those parameters define. None of Q-01 (which error the owner prefers), Q-02 (detecting a changed network context) or Q-03 (retention) covers them.
findings.evidence: 08.02.02-route-aware-radius-correction.md:26 — '`[PARTIAL]` — the arbitration rule is the substance of this feature and it is genuinely undecided.' Line 42-43 — '`[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`: the actual confidence model, the sample thresholds, the decay rate on old probes, and whether corrections are per-route or per-peer.' The dependent states, lines 68-70 — '| Predicted | No usable history | … | Learning | Some history, below confidence threshold | Estimate + "refining based on N sessions" | Measured | Confidence threshold met | Hard boundary + sample count + last-updated |'. Sibling threshold questions in this domain were routed explicitly rather than left pending — 08.05.02-take-alignment-drift-correction.md:322 (Q-06) routes the 1/5/20 ms tier boundaries to '`/create-prd-compile` (performance budget)', and 08.06-session-preflight-rig-readiness.md:122 (Q-03) routes pre-flight staleness to the same place.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer picks a threshold — say three probes — and a user whose ISP had one bad evening crosses it. Their radius hardens to a measured boundary drawn from a transient fault, which 08.02.02 D-02 exists to prevent ('A single anomalous probe permanently shrinking a radius is the naive implementation's defining bug'), and because the same value feeds the exported predicate (CX-02), they become invisible in Community, Opportunities, Services and Education searches on evidence they cannot see or contest.

findings.claim: Whether a materially shrunk radius notifies the user is deferred circularly: the feature file defers to the parent CX, and the parent CX defers the same item to Step 5. Both markers name a stage that has completed and neither carries an owner.
findings.evidence: 08.02.02-route-aware-radius-correction.md:60 — '| Correction shrinks the radius materially | Bad news the user did not ask for. Whether to notify is a real product question — see parent CX-01. | `[PENDING — Step 5]` |'. 08.02-playable-radius-peer-matching-cx.md:36 (CX-01 synthesis Q4) — '`[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — whether a materially shrunk radius notifies the user. It is bad news about their own connection and there is a real argument both ways.' The feature's own D-04 makes the omission sharper: 'Corrections are explained by cause, not just shown as a number | "Your radius shrank" is alarming; "your ISP routes you the long way round" is actionable.'
findings.failure_scenario: The one file that could answer the question points at the file that points back at it, and the shared deferral target no longer exists as a future stage. D-04 specifies how a correction must be explained but not whether the user is ever told, so an implementer building only what is specified renders the explanation on a screen the user has no reason to open — and someone's discoverability shrinks with no event they ever see, which CX-02's role scoping calls 'the sharpest edge in the sub-domain'.

findings.forcedInvention: Whether the two features that carry this domain's media-infrastructure cost are v1 Musts or deferred Shoulds.
findings.claim: Two files in this unit state, as the cited resolution of a live question, that MoSCoW placed 08.03.01 and 08.03.02 in the MUST bucket. The cited ledger places both under SHOULD. The quoted rationale text is genuine; the bucket label attached to it is not.
findings.evidence: 08.03-remote-monitoring-session-attendance-index.md:61 (Q-03) — 'MoSCoW then placed 08.03.01 and 08.03.02 in [moscow-ledger.md](../../moscow-ledger.md) § **MUST (195)** under the domain-08 path.' And 08.03.01-hifi-monitor-stream-quality-contract.md:126 (Q-03) — 'MoSCoW then placed this feature in [moscow-ledger.md](../../moscow-ledger.md) § **MUST (195)** under the domain-08 path — "The one part of domain 08 with proven willingness to pay … Crucially it is latency-TOLERANT".' The ledger says otherwise: ideation/moscow-ledger.md line 291 ('| 08.03.01 | High-Fidelity Monitor Stream & Quality Contract | … | The one part of domain 08 with proven willingness to') and line 292 ('| 08.03.02 | Listener Roster, Invite Links & Access Windows | … | Ships with monitoring — the stream cannot exist without it') both fall under '## SHOULD (285)' (line 217); the '## MUST (195)' section spans lines 17-216 and contains only 08.05.01, 08.05.02, 08.05.04 and 08.07 from this domain (lines 80-83).
findings.failure_scenario: Domain Q-03 is the domain's central risk — 'Everything except Overdub Mode needs media infrastructure that meta/constraints.md does not have' (realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-index.md:132) — and 08.07 sharpens it to 'the mode is free on the locked stack, the witness is what costs media infrastructure'. A v1 scope built from these two files makes the monitor stream and its roster Musts, which forces dedicated media infrastructure into v1 and breaks the locked Astro/Cloudflare/Supabase stack. The ledger's actual placement (Should) keeps the four true Musts — capture, alignment, attendance, overdub — entirely on the locked stack. The two readings produce different v1 architectures and different answers to the owner's open stack decision.

findings.evidence: 08.03.04-monitoring-trust-playback-context.md:51-53 — '`[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`: whether any detection is acceptable; how the tension warning is worded …; whether the listener sees their own context assessment.' A reviewer checking against D-01 rejects it, and the round-trip exists only because a decision and a pending marker on the same page disagree.

findings.forcedInvention: When a declared playback context becomes stale, and what a stale declaration shows.
findings.claim: A named state in the States table has `[PENDING]` in both its trigger and its user-visible column, and the edge case that produces it is also `[PENDING — Step 5]`. Step 5 has completed, no owner is recorded, and none of the file's three open questions covers staleness — while D-04 forbids the obvious fallback of assuming a default.
findings.evidence: 08.03.04-monitoring-trust-playback-context.md:79 — '| Stale | `[PENDING — Step 5]` | `[PENDING]` |'. And line 69 — '| Listener changes their playback mid-session (unplugs headphones) | The declaration is now stale and nothing knows. Realistic and common. | `[PENDING — Step 5]` |'. Against line 104 (D-04) — 'Undeclared means unknown, never an assumed default | An inferred context is confidently wrong, which is worse than an admitted gap.' The file's open questions are Q-01 (is this a real product), Q-02 (read from domains 15/16 instead of asking) and Q-03 (warning wording) — none addresses staleness.
findings.failure_scenario: A client declares studio monitors, then unplugs and finishes the session on laptop speakers. The tension-warning logic (Happy Path step 4) keeps evaluating notes against the stale declaration, so a genuine low-end complaint from laptop speakers arrives with no caveat while a valid note is caveated — the feature's single output inverted. The system is presenting an inferred-current context, which is precisely what D-04 calls 'confidently wrong', and nothing in the spec tells the implementer to expire or re-ask.

An implementer satisfies D-03 with a passive roster panel nobody looks at while playing; a label rep joins mid-take and the performer never notices, which is functionally the anonymous listening DT-02 rejected as 'a request to deceive someone about who is hearing them play'.

findings.forcedInvention: How a high volume of live listener notes is collapsed or batched for the Producer.
findings.claim: The file states that collapsing or batching 'is needed' and leaves both the mechanism and the user-visible result at `[PENDING — Step 5]`, with no owner, after Step 5 completed, and with no covering open question (Q-01 is the commenting grant, Q-02 is performer visibility, Q-03 is the highlight-flag merge).
findings.evidence: 08.03.03-live-listener-feedback-notes.md:58 — '| High note volume from an enthusiastic client | The Producer is running a session, not a ticket queue. Some collapsing or batching is needed. | `[PENDING — Step 5]` |'. The constraint it must satisfy is fixed at line 93 (D-02) — 'Notes never interrupt a performer mid-take' — and at line 39-40 — 'a note must never interrupt a performer mid-take. Anything that pops up in front of someone who is playing is a defect wearing a feature's clothes.'
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer ships an unbatched note stream. A client leaving fifteen notes across one take produces fifteen anchored items competing for the Producer's attention while they are running the session — and the Producer is routinely also playing (the multi-hyphenate case the domain treats as structural), so the surface the file wanted 'invisible until used' becomes the loudest thing on screen at the moment D-02 is trying to protect.

findings.claim: The Musician is marked 'Read-only' on 08.04.01 in both Role Matrix and Role Lens, but the same Role Lens grants them a persisted write — setting their own talkback intrusion level — and the sub-domain CX stores that value in their portable profile. Read-only contradicts the described capability; the domain uses 'Config' for exactly this kind of self-scoped declaration elsewhere.
findings.evidence: 08.04-talkback-cue-mixes-index.md:37 — '| 08.04.01 Talkback Channel & Ducking | 👁️ Read-only | ✅ Full | ⚙️ Config | ❌ None |'. 08.04.01-talkback-channel-ducking.md:21 — 'Musician | Read-only | … Sets how much talkback intrudes into their own mix (their monitoring is theirs, per parent D-02) but cannot mute the engineer entirely'. Confirmed as a persisted value at 08.04-talkback-cue-mixes-cx.md:12 (CX-03) — 'Talkback level is part of the performer's monitoring preference — some want the engineer loud, some want minimal ducking. It travels with the profile.' And 08.04.03-cue-mix-recall-portable-profile.md:40 — '| Talkback ducking depth | Property of the person, not the room |'. Contrast the domain's own use of Config for a self-scoped declaration: 08.03.04-monitoring-trust-playback-context.md:26 — 'Musician | Config | Declares their own playback chain'.
findings.failure_scenario: A permission model generated from the Role Matrix denies the Musician any write on the talkback feature. The talkback intrusion level then becomes unsettable by the person who owns it — contradicting index D-02 ('The performer owns their own cue mix; the Producer can help but not override') — and 08.04.03's portable profile has a slot it can store but nobody can populate, so recall restores a preference that could never be set.

findings.claim: The sub-domain CX leaves CX-03's synthesis at `[PENDING — Step 5]` with no owner after Step 5 completed, and the specific 'open part' it names has in fact already been decided by 08.04.01 D-03 in the same unit.
findings.evidence: 08.04-talkback-cue-mixes-cx.md:61-64 (CX-03) — '`[PARTIAL]` … The open part is whether a performer may carry a *minimal ducking* preference into a room where the Producer needs to be heard, which is a small instance of the same authority question CX-01 answers.' Line 71 — '**Synthesis questions answered**: `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — Medium confidence, deferred per the CX template's rule for non-High entries.' Already decided at 08.04.01-talkback-channel-ducking.md:95 (D-03) — 'Performers control talkback's intrusion level but cannot mute it | Their monitoring is theirs; their reachability is the session's.' — with the mechanism given at line 59: 'Performer mutes talkback entirely | Not permitted. … | Level control bottoms out above silence.'
findings.failure_scenario: The CX is the file a Step-6 or PRD reader consults for inter-feature authority questions. It presents as open a question its own child already answered with a floor mechanism, so the reader either re-litigates a settled decision or, reading only the CX, concludes the profile may carry an unbounded minimal-ducking preference into a live room — which would let a performer make themselves unreachable by profile, the outcome D-03 exists to prevent.

findings.forcedInvention: Whether the attendance record produced by an overdub is the same record as a live session's, or a lower-graded one.
findings.claim: 08.05.04's Cross-Cut Notes still assert that the attendance record 'works identically' under Overdub Mode. The same file's Behavior table and edge-case table say the opposite — delivery-certainty, not performance-certainty, at a per-segment grade. Both statements are unmarked and unqualified, in one file, with no open question over either.
findings.evidence: 08.05.04-session-attendance-provenance.md:218 — '- **Works identically under 08.07 Overdub Mode** ([../08.07-overdub-mode.md]) — which is why this survives even if the real-time rooms are cut (domain D-05, D-06).' Contradicted by the same file at line 50 — '| Provenance grade | A live-room segment is `observed-playing`; an overdub is `delivered-by` by default and becomes `observed-playing` only for segments a live witness observed (CX-09) | `delivered-by` establishes delivery, not performance |' — and at line 166 — '| Overdub session (no real-time room) | The record has delivery-certainty, not performance-certainty … It becomes `observed-playing` only for segments a live witness observed (CX-09); the grade is per-segment, so an unwitnessed segment remains `delivered-by`. |'. And externally by 08.07-overdub-mode.md:353 (D-04) — 'NOT identically to a live session' — and realtime-jamming-remote-sessions-cx.md:23 (CX-07) — '08.05.04's "overdub works identically → same record" edge is **wrong** and must be corrected.'
findings.failure_scenario: The Step-6 correction landed in this file's Behavior and edge tables but not in its Cross-Cut Notes, so the file now states both positions. The Cross-Cut Notes are the section a cross-layer reader (and the 08.05.04 → 08.07 and 08.05.04 → 02.04.02 edges) reads for inter-feature contracts. An implementer taking the line-218 contract builds one record type and no grade field; the tier model in 02.04.02 then receives an unwitnessed solo overdub — which 08.07 line 259 describes as indistinguishable from a ghost-played or generated file — carrying the same weight as a live session the platform observed end to end. That is the 'verified false credit' 08.05.04 DT-02 names as worse than an unverified one, produced by the feature whose entire stated value is that it 'observes rather than claims'.

findings.forcedInvention: Whether the presence-to-contribution bridge is defined or still open.
findings.claim: The sub-domain CX states that the highlights↔attendance relationship 'is genuinely unresolved and is the substance of index Q-01', but index Q-01 is marked RESOLVED and specifies the three-component bridge. The CX's synthesis is additionally left at `[PENDING — Step 5]` with no owner after Step 5 completed.
findings.evidence: 08.05-session-capture-recall-cx.md:86 (CX-04) — 'Highlights are the signal that separates "was in the room" from "is on the record". The exact relationship is genuinely unresolved and is the substance of index Q-01.' Line 94 — '**Synthesis questions answered**: `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — Medium confidence … Flagged as consequential: this is where an over-eager inference could manufacture or erase a credit.' Contradicted by 08.05-session-capture-recall-index.md:64 (Q-01) — '**RESOLVED — it never does.** … the presence→contribution bridge is kept material (08.05.03) + attestation (`02.04.01`) + declaration (`02.06`), and presence alone contributes zero.' And by 08.05.04-session-attendance-provenance.md:77-86, which tabulates the three bridge components and states '**Presence alone contributes zero** … That is the design, not a gap.' 08.05.04's own Cross-Cut Notes line 204 confirm the CX entry is answerable: 'See CX-04, now answerable: highlights supply the *contribution* signal, this supplies the *identity* signal, and `02.04.02` combines them.'
findings.failure_scenario: A reader working from the CX — the file whose whole job is to hold inter-feature relationships — sees the most consequential relationship in the sub-domain marked unresolved and pending a stage that has ended. They either re-open a settled decision or, worse, treat the bridge as undesigned and invent a weighting from highlights to credit, which is the 'over-eager inference could manufacture or erase a credit' the same paragraph warns about and which 08.05.04 D-02 and DT-09 both forbid.

findings.forcedInvention: The length of the retrospective flag window, and whether it is adjustable by the person flagging.
findings.claim: The decision fixes the window's anchor (it ends at the gesture) but never states its duration or adjustability, and no open question covers it — while the file's own DT-01 cites a category idiom with a specific number without adopting it.
findings.evidence: 08.05.03-auto-highlights-moment-flagging.md:105 (D-01) — 'A flag anchors to a retrospective window ending at the gesture | Humans flag after realising. See DT-01.' Line 66 — '| Flag placed late (they realised after it happened) | The normal case, not an edge case. A flag means "the thing that just happened", so it must anchor to a window *before* the gesture, not at it. | Flag creates a region ending at the gesture, not starting there. |'. The number is named only as someone else's convention, at line 88 (DT-01) — 'this is exactly why retrospective record exists on hardware loopers and why "capture the last 30 seconds" is the standard idiom for this problem.' The file's three open questions are Q-01 (are flags private or shared), Q-02 (is audio analysis in scope) and Q-03 (merge with 08.03.03) — none is the window.
findings.failure_scenario: Two implementers pick different windows. A ten-second window misses the take a player flagged four bars after it ended; a two-minute window hands the Producer a region containing the flagged passage plus the two failed attempts before it, which makes the flag no better than the unflagged session and defeats D-02's premise that manual flagging is the reliable signal. The region length is what the Producer actually reviews, so it is product behaviour, not tuning — and unlike the domain's other numeric gaps (08.05.02 Q-06, 08.06 Q-03, 08.01.02 Q-01) it is routed nowhere.
